events.title: Copper cable hit with Sec. 232 tariffs by…?
events.description:
HTSUS statistical line 8544.49.3040 targets insulated copper conductors, over 600V up to 1,000V, not fitted with connectors.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if a legally operative Section 232 instrument subjects all articles under this line to a duty above 0%, a tariff-rate quota, an absolute quota, or another quantitative restriction by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

For the purposes of this market, legally operative Section 232 instruments include but are not limited to: a presidential proclamation, a Commerce-USTR determination under that proclamation's clause 11 process, another Federal Register or chapter 99 action under Section 232 authority, or an Act of Congress.

A qualifying instrument may name the line itself or any broader provision that fully includes it (e.g., tariff line 8544.49.30, subheading 8544.49, or heading 8544). If USITC renumbers the line, its successor will count the same way.

A qualifying instrument must be enacted, signed, or otherwise put into legal operation by the specified date, regardless of whether the instrument stipulates a later date of enforcement.

Tariff imposition will qualify regardless of whether there exist 0% in-quota rates, country carve-outs, metal-content thresholds, phased effective dates, or other conditions.

Only tariffs imposed on HTSUS statistical line 8544.49.3040 will qualify. Coverage of only a subset or end use (e.g., wind-turbine or data-center cable only), additions limited to sister line 8544.49.3080, investigation steps, reports, proposals, or announcements without a signed operative instrument, one chamber passage, instruments whose only effect is a 0% rate or an exemption, and tariffs under any other authority (e.g., Section 301, IEEPA, AD/CVD, reciprocal) will not qualify.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the US government.

events.title: U.S. tariff rate on China on December 31, 2026?
events.description:
This market will resolve according to the general tariff rate on imports into the United States from the People's Republic of China on December 31, 2026, 12:00 PM ET.

The general tariff rate refers to the base tariff rate paid on imports, including any general tariff the U.S. imposes on all imports (e.g. a 10% tariff on all U.S. imports and a 10% tariff on top of that on Chinese imports would equal a 20% tariff).

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

Item specific exceptions or increases will not be considered (i.e. this market does not refer to the effective tariff rate).

Only tariffs which are in effect will qualify. Tariffs which are paused, or which have been announced but have not yet gone into effect will not be considered.

This market's primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration, however a consensus of credible information will also be used.

events.title: Tariff increase on Canada in effect by...?
events.description:
On January 24, President Trump announced that the United States would apply a 100% tariff to all imports from Canada if a trade deal with China goes through. (see: https://www.reuters.com/world/china/trump-threatens-canada-with-100-tariff-over-possible-deal-with-china-2026-01-24/).

This market will resolve to “Yes” if an increase in the general tariff rate on imports into the United States from Canada goes into effect for any amount of time by June 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

For the purpose of this market, "goes into effect" means the start date of the tariffs (as set by legislation or executive action) must have passed without being further delayed or suspended. Only tariffs which are in effect will qualify. Tariffs which are paused, or which have been announced but not yet gone into effect will not be considered.

Only tariffs specifically targeting Canada will qualify. For example, a new global tariff (tariffs on all imports into the U.S.) will not count toward this market's resolution.

The general tariff rate refers to the base tariff rate paid on imports, including any general tariff the U.S. imposes on all imports (e.g. a 10% tariff on all U.S. imports and a 50% tariff on top of that on Canadian imports would equal a 60% tariff). Item specific exceptions will not be considered (i.e. this market does not refer to the effective tariff rate). For the purpose of this market, an increase in the general tariff rate is defined as a rate greater than the rate in effect at the time of this market's creation.

A general tariff that includes item specific exceptions will still qualify, as long as a policy of a general tariff on all imports into the United States from Canada is in effect which is greater than the policy in effect at the time of this market's creation.

This market's primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration; however, a consensus of credible information will also be used.

events.title: Canadian unwrought aluminum duty rate on December 31, 2027?
events.description:
This market will resolve according to the Section 232 duty rate applicable to Canadian unwrought aluminum as of 12:01 AM ET on December 31, 2027.

“Canadian unwrought aluminum” refers to unwrought aluminum not alloyed (HTSUS subheading 7601.10), that is a product of Canada and for which Canada is both the country of smelt and the country of most recent cast.

Only the rate applicable generally to Canadian unwrought aluminum will be considered. Company-specific or project-specific reduced rates, product exclusions, and special rates for US-origin metal will not be considered. Ordinary customs duties, Section 338 duties, antidumping and countervailing duties, and any other tariff will not be considered. If a tariff-rate quota applies, the in-quota rate will be used, whether or not the quota has been filled at the measurement time. If different general rates apply to different goods within subheading 7601.10, the lowest of those rates will be used.

Only the rate legally in effect at the measurement time counts. A change that has been announced or signed but is not in effect as of 12:01 AM ET on December 31, 2027 will not be considered. A change which goes into effect at that time will qualify. A change signed after the measurement time will not be considered, even if it is made retroactive to a date on or before December 31, 2027.

If Section 232 aluminum duties do not apply to Canadian unwrought aluminum at the measurement time for any reason, including an exemption, a termination, a suspension, or a court order that is in effect and has not been stayed, the market will resolve to “0%“.

If the Section 232 duty rate applicable to Canadian unwrought aluminum in effect as of 12:01 AM ET on December 31, 2027 is not expressed solely as an ad valorem percentage, including where it is a specific duty or a combination of a percentage and a specific duty, this market will resolve to “Other.”

The primary resolution sources will be presidential proclamations and executive orders published on whitehouse.gov and in the Federal Register, Federal Register notices issued under them, and HTSUS Chapter 99 as published by the US International Trade Commission. If these sources conflict, the most recent legally effective proclamation, executive order, or Federal Register notice will govern, followed by the HTSUS, and then the US Customs and Border Protection CSMS guidance.

events.title: US-Canada deal to cut Section 338 tariffs by December 30?
events.description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if by December 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, both of the following occur: i) the United States and Canada announce a qualifying diplomatic agreement to lower or remove the Section 338 tariffs on Canada; and ii) the President of the United States signs a qualifying executive action that terminates, suspends, or reduces the Section 338 tariffs on Canada, on or after the date of the first qualifying announcement. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The Section 338 Proclamations refers to the three presidential proclamations signed on July 20, 2026 under Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 that impose an additional 50% duty on specified products of Canada, as amended by any later proclamation.

A qualifying diplomatic agreement refers to an official agreement, treaty, deal, framework, arrangement, or substantially similar diplomatic instrument between the United States and Canada, including a multilateral agreement to which both are parties, that commits or obligates the United States to lower or remove the additional duties imposed under the Section 338 Proclamations, or includes the lowering or removal of those duties as part of its stated terms. The agreement does not need to reference Section 338 by name, provided its terms cover the additional duties imposed under the Section 338 Proclamations. An agreement that only lowers or removes other US tariffs on Canada will not qualify, including Section 232 tariffs on goods that are also covered by the Section 338 Proclamations. An agreement in principle, or a framework subject to further finalization, will qualify provided the accepted terms include the lowering or removal of the additional duties imposed under the Section 338 Proclamations. An agreement only to begin or continue negotiations, or one that sets a process or timetable for reaching a deal, will not qualify.

Both countries must announce their acceptance of the same qualifying diplomatic agreement. A joint announcement will qualify, as will separate announcements from each country of its own acceptance of an agreement which, taken together, directly indicate that both countries accepted the same agreement. Qualifying announcements must come from the US government (the President, the White House, the Office of the United States Trade Representative, or the Department of Commerce) and from the Government of Canada (the Prime Minister, the Office of the Prime Minister, Global Affairs Canada, the Department of Finance Canada, or any federal minister speaking on behalf of the Government of Canada). Statements posted by the President or the Prime Minister on their official or personal social media accounts will count. Separate announcements of individual policies will not qualify if the policies are not announced as part of a diplomatic agreement.

Each announcement must be a declarative statement that clearly and unambiguously communicates acceptance of an agreement. Statements that merely reference ongoing negotiations or a prospective agreement, or that allude to or express support for an agreement without confirming acceptance of a qualifying agreement, do not qualify. An announcement of the acceptance of an agreement in principle or a framework whose accepted terms include the lowering or removal of the additional duties imposed under the Section 338 Proclamations will not be treated as referencing ongoing negotiations or a prospective agreement, even if further terms, legal text, or domestic approvals remain to be finalized. A qualifying announcement need not reference the agreement by name or use specific terminology, provided it clearly communicates acceptance of an agreement.

Whether announcements from the United States and Canada represent a diplomatic agreement, and whether such an agreement qualifies, will be determined through the announcements themselves, the text of the agreement, further announcements from either country, and a consensus of credible reporting, including information published after the initial announcements. If, by the deadline, both countries have made potentially qualifying announcements and a qualifying executive action has been signed, but it remains ambiguous whether the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement, this market will remain open until either i) definitive confirmation is achieved through the sources above or ii) 14 calendar days (ET) have passed after the deadline. If, at the end of the fourteenth calendar day, no definitive confirmation has been achieved, the announcements will be adjudicated based on the totality of information available from the resolution sources at that time. No single statement, denial, or presentation of evidence will govern where it is contradicted by the totality of information.

A qualifying executive action refers to a presidential proclamation or executive order signed by the President of the United States and published on the White House presidential actions page or in the Federal Register that, for goods covered by the Section 338 Proclamations, either i) terminates the additional duty imposed under at least one of the Section 338 Proclamations in full, or suspends it in full with no stated end date or with a stated end date at least 90 days after the suspension begins; or ii) lowers the additional duty rate imposed under at least one of the Section 338 Proclamations below 50% for all goods covered by that proclamation. A reduced rate that applies only up to a quota volume will qualify, provided the reduced rate is available for all goods covered by that proclamation. The action must be signed on or after the date of the first qualifying announcement. The date the action is signed will be used, regardless of when the change takes effect. An action signed by the deadline but published afterward will count, provided it is published within 14 calendar days (ET) after the deadline. Other executive actions, including presidential memoranda, statements, and announcements, will not qualify.

The following will not qualify as a qualifying executive action: changes to the product lists or scope of the Section 338 Proclamations; product-specific or company-specific exclusions; a suspension with a stated end date fewer than 90 days after it begins, including successive shorter suspensions that together exceed 90 days; a court ruling that invalidates, enjoins, or otherwise blocks the tariffs; changes to import bans imposed under Section 338; changes to Section 232 tariffs or any other tariff.

This market will resolve to “Yes” as soon as both conditions have been met.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be presidential actions published on the White House website (https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/) and in the Federal Register, and official information from the governments of the United States and Canada; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

events.title: Will Trump create a $5,000 dividend by March 31, 2027?
events.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Trump Administration formally creates a general dividend, rebate, or stimulus payment meeting the criteria below by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, whether by signing federal legislation, by executive action, or by any other official mechanism. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Any bill enacted into law or executive action taken within this market's time frame will qualify, regardless of when the law or action goes into effect. 

To qualify, the payment must be for an amount of at least $5,000 per recipient and must be distributed to a broad segment of individual US taxpayers. A payment is "broad" if eligibility for it extends to at least a majority (50%) of U.S. individual taxpayers, or if eligibility is limited only by general income thresholds and/or household or filing status rather than by any narrower category. 

The payment must be established as a new, distinct dividend, rebate, or stimulus payment. A payment structured as a new refundable tax credit, an advance payment of a new credit, or a direct disbursement by the Treasury will qualify, regardless of the legal mechanism used to deliver it. An increase to, expansion of, or acceleration of a tax credit, deduction, or refund that existed as of market creation, will not qualify.

Once a qualifying law or executive action has been created within the market's time frame, this market will resolve to "Yes" regardless of whether it is later repealed, enjoined, or never results in any payment actually being made.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting, supported where available by official information from the U.S. government.

events.title: US Trade Deficit in 2026?
events.description:
This market will resolve according to the annual US Goods and Services Deficit for 2026, as reported by the US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) and the US Census Bureau (USCB) in the “U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services” release for December and Annual 2026, expected to be released in February 2027.

Upon publication, the specified release will be made available at: https://www.bea.gov/news/current-releases

The relevant figure may be found in the annual summary under “Exports, Imports, and Balance (exhibit 1)”. Changes in the BEA or USCB’s reporting format will not disqualify a relevant published figure from counting.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the “U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services” release for December and Annual 2026 from the US Bureau of Economic Analysis and the US Census Bureau. If this release is not published by April 30, 2027 ET, another credible source on the annual US Goods and Services Deficit for 2026 will be chosen.

Note: any revisions to the annual US Goods and Services Deficit for 2026 made after the publication of the “U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services” release for December and Annual 2026 will not be considered.
